forecast-period.text: Showers lingering behind a cold front in Bass Strait will ease this morning. A high pressure system will then move over the Bight today, and will extend a ridge across the state as it slowly moves east into NSW by Saturday. Another cold front is then forecast to cross the state from Saturday evening into Sunday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Possible morning fog patches in the southwest. Isolated showers about the Agricultural Area, particularly about windward facing coasts and ranges. Small hail is possible with early morning showers in the far southeast. Maximum temperatures below average. Southeast to southwesterly winds, tending easterly in the west.

Possible morning fog and frost on and east of the ranges. Chance of isolated light showers about the Southern Agricultural Area. Maximum temperatures below average. Variable winds across the southeast, tending northeast to southeasterly winds in the north.

Possible morning fog and frost about the Agricultural Area on and east of the ranges, and possible frost about the North West Pastoral. Light morning showers about southern coasts and ranges are possible. Maximum temperatures average to below average. Northeast to southeasterly winds, tending variable in the southeast.

text.p: Possible morning frost about the Eyre Peninsula and northern inland parts. Mostly dry. Maximum temperatures below average. North to northeasterly winds.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Saturday: Less than 2 mm about the Northern Agricultural Area and south of the Pastoral districts, with falls between 2 to 5 mm about the Southern Agricultural Area. Isolated falls of 5 to 10 mm possible about windward facing coasts and ranges and the southern coast of the Lower South East.
